key_insight: This paper explores whether self-distillation can work without any privileged answers or extra visual evidence, relying only on input conditioning to create a useful learning signal. The goal is a simpler form of on-policy self-distillation that keeps the benefits of asymmetry without requiring additional supervision.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of how to make a self-teacher consistently stronger than the student in on-policy self-distillation, without depending on external teachers, privileged labels, or extra visual cues.
method: Investigate input-conditioning as the only source of asymmetry between teacher and student.
Remove the need for privileged answers and visual evidence used by prior OPSD methods.
Design a self-distillation setup where the teacher signal is generated directly from conditioned inputs on-policy.
impact: If successful, this approach could make self-distillation simpler, cheaper, and easier to deploy in real systems. It may reduce dependence on extra supervision while preserving training stability and performance gains.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline showing traditional OPD vs. OPSD vs. input-conditioned self-distillation
Diagram of teacher-student information flow highlighting the removed privileged inputs
Simple block illustration of asymmetric conditioning creating a stronger teacher signal
Icons for 'no external teacher', 'no privileged answers', and 'no extra visual evidence'
paper_authors: Yijun Liang, Yunjie Tian, Yijiang Li, Yuqi Jia, Furong Huang
